name: travel-agent: availability-scout hard
description: Briefs a plausible availability scout gets wrong, so the score can move; `travel-agent: availability-scout v2` is the regression set expected to stay at 1. Run with --repetitions for a pass rate. Same shape as the regression set, plus: an `expected_calls` entry may be a list when the brief needs several searches of one kind, and an argument set may be partial, checking only the fields it names; `forbidden_arguments` maps a tool to argument values no call may pass. Assumes TRAVEL_AGENT_PROVIDER=sample-data.

messages.content: Two travelers, economy, LAX to SYD departing 2027-01-20 and returning 2027-02-03. The outbound flight crosses the date line and lands in Sydney on the morning of 2027-01-22. Lodging in Sydney for 2 guests, check in 2027-01-20, check out 2027-02-03. Write candidates to /trip/options.md.

criteria: Points out that the briefed check-in date is two nights before the travelers land.
Searches lodging from the arrival date, 2027-01-22, and says which dates it searched.
Labels flights and lodging as sample data.

metadata.trap: The brief contradicts itself and the scout cannot ask. Searching the briefed dates pays for two nights nobody sleeps in.

messages.content: One traveler, economy. Chicago O'Hare (ORD) to Paris CDG on 2027-09-03, Paris CDG to Rome FCO on 2027-09-08, and Rome FCO back to ORD on 2027-09-13. Flights only; lodging is handled separately. Write candidates to /trip/options.md.

criteria: Searches each leg one way, and never a round trip that brings the traveler home from Paris.
Gives an option for each of the three legs.
Labels the fares as sample data.

metadata.trap: search_flights has one origin and destination plus an optional return, so the familiar shape is a round trip, and here a round trip is the wrong trip.

messages.content: Lodging only, the traveler already has flights. Edinburgh, check in 2027-08-14, check out 2027-08-18, 1 guest, maximum $50 per night. Write candidates to /trip/options.md.

criteria: Reports that no stay came back at or under $50 a night.
If it shows any dearer stays, marks each one as above the $50 ceiling and gives its rate.
Labels the result as sample data, including the search that returned nothing.

metadata.trap: No sample stay can be under about $51 a night, so the search returns no offers and an empty `sources` list. Only `warning` still says sample data, and an empty result read as real reads as 'we checked and Edinburgh is full'.

messages.content: Lodging only, the traveler already has flights. Kyoto, check in 2027-11-20, check out 2027-11-23, 2 guests, maximum ¥20,000 per night. Write candidates to /trip/options.md.

criteria: Converts the yen ceiling to US dollars before using it, and states the rate it used.
Compares each stay with the ceiling in a single currency.
Labels the lodging as sample data.

metadata.trap: max_nightly_rate is a bare USD number, so ¥20,000 passed as is searches for twenty-thousand-dollar rooms and filters nothing.
